root_cause.text: The btusb driver uses devm_kzalloc() to allocate the shared `btusb_data` structure, which ties its lifetime to a single USB interface (`intf`), but the structure is accessed by multiple interfaces (INTF, ISOC, DIAG); when one interface is disconnected, devm frees the memory prematurely while other interfaces still reference it, leading to use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message states: "In btusb_probe(), we use devm_kzalloc() to allocate the btusb data. This ties the lifetime of all the btusb data to the binding of a driver to one interface, INTF. In a driver that binds to other interfaces, ISOC and DIAG, this is an accident waiting to happen. The issue is revealed in btusb_disconnect(), where calling usb_driver_release_interface(&btusb_driver, data->intf) will have devm free the data that is also being used by the other interfaces of the driver that may not be released yet." The patch reverts to explicit `kzalloc` and adds `kfree(data)` in error paths and `btusb_disconnect()`.

candidates.rationale: Allocates btusb_data using devm_kzalloc tied to a single USB interface (intf), but the structure is shared across multiple interfaces. When one interface disconnects, devm frees the memory prematurely while other interfaces still reference it, causing use-after-free.

Stores a pointer to the devm-managed btusb_data in hdev. If data is freed due to another interface's disconnect, this pointer becomes dangling, leading to use-after-free when the HCI core accesses it via hdev.
Assigns a receive callback to the shared data structure. After the data is freed prematurely, this callback pointer becomes invalid if invoked on another interface.
Accesses endpoint fields of the shared data. If data is freed by another interface's disconnect while this check runs (e.g., during probe of a secondary interface), it results in use-after-free.
Sets a command request type on the shared data. If data is freed before this assignment completes on a different interface, it writes to freed memory.
Accesses data->reset_gpio in an error path. If data is freed by a concurrent disconnect of another interface, this becomes a use-after-free read.

Frees the HCI device device. This may be called after the shared data is freed, but hdev still holds a reference to the dangling data, potentially causing double-free or use-after-free in subsequent cleanup.
